Hoagie Rolls Baker's Percentage

Divide this batch into 8 long rolls of 103 g. Proof them seam-side down, then bake until the crust can hold a filling.

Detailed method

The calculator opens at 500 g flour, 62% hydration, 2% salt, and 0.8% yeast. That is 310 g water, 10 g salt, and 4 g yeast, 824 g of dough. The balls fields open at 8 rolls of 103 g. Shape long rolls, proof them seam-side down, and bake until the crust can hold a filling. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 310 g water, 10 g salt, and 4 g instant yeast, then knead for about 8 minutes until smooth. At 62% the dough is soft and holds a ball. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 70 to 90 minutes. With 0.8% yeast it should about double.
  3. Divide Divide the 824 g dough into 8 pieces of 103 g, the weight in the balls fields. Cover them and rest 10 minutes.
  4. Shape Roll each piece into a log about 18 cm long and pinch the seam shut. Set the rolls seam-side down on a sheet, with a little space between them.
  5. Proof Cover the rolls for 30 to 45 minutes, until they look puffy. Keep the seam underneath.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 200°C (390°F). Bake 16 to 20 minutes, until the crust is golden and firm enough to hold a filling. The top may split as they bake, the way the rolls in the photo do.
  7. Cool Set them on a rack for at least 15 minutes before you split one lengthwise.
